title: Norm Level Vocabulary
description: Single source of truth for the hierarchy of norms (ADR-0033). A norm's `level` says which rank of the legal order it occupies; `rank` orders those levels so that subordination is computable rather than prose. LOWER rank = HIGHER authority: a norm at rank 30 (federal) outranks one at rank 50 (municipal), and a municipal ordinance is therefore subordinate to every level with a lower rank that shares its lineage. Consumers (legal-search projection builder, norm-hierarchy endpoint, platform-control jurisdiction seeds) MUST read the ordering from here and not restate it. Levels are 10 apart so intermediate ranks (e.g. a cantonal-constitutional tier) can be inserted without renumbering.

constitutional.description: The constitution of a federal jurisdiction (CH: Bundesverfassung, SR 101). NOT derivable from the jurisdiction alone — the BV is enacted by the same federal jurisdiction as an ordinary statute but outranks it — so it is the one level a document declares explicitly, overriding the level inherited from its jurisdiction.

international.description: Treaty law and EU law (jur_eu). CAVEAT: the rank of international law relative to ordinary federal statutes is contested in Swiss doctrine. It is placed above federal statutes here per the monist reading of BV Art. 5(4); consumers that need the Schubert-Praxis exception must not read this rank as settled law.

federal.description: Statutes and ordinances of a national/federal jurisdiction (CH: jur_ch_federal — TSchG, TSchV; also the national-container jurisdictions jur_ch, jur_de, jur_at, jur_fr, jur_it).

cantonal.description: Law of a sub-federal subdivision: Swiss cantons (jur_ch_zh — Hundegesetz) and German Länder (jur_de_by). The label is Swiss-first; the level covers every ISO 3166-2 subdivision tier in contracts/vocabularies/subdivisions.json.

municipal.description: Law of a commune (jur_ch_gemeinde_261 — the Zurich Hundereglement). Communal norms hold only delegated competence: they are valid only where a cantonal norm delegates the competence to legislate, which is why `delegates_to` — not merely `subordinate_to` — is what decides whether a municipal ban is authorised.
